prompt: Simulate round-robin serving with an ArrayDeque queue: each person gets one turn per rotation and leaves the queue when their needs reach zero. Return the order in which people finish.
explanation: An ArrayDeque used with removeFirst and addLast behaves as a FIFO queue, which models a waiting line naturally. Queueing array indexes instead of names lets one int array track how many turns each person still needs; cloning that array keeps the caller's input untouched. Each loop iteration serves exactly one turn, so a person cycles to the back until their count hits zero.
hints: Put the indexes 0..names.length-1 into an ArrayDeque<Integer>; removeFirst and addLast give queue behavior.
Clone the needs array (needs.clone()) so you can decrement counts without mutating the input.
Loop while the queue is not empty: take the front index, decrement its count, then either record the name or addLast the index back.
